partners.name: Sustain-Nobility

asked.by: Dinis, met at the summit; relayed by attendees.1.fringe@PrompTugal.dinis

partners.one_line: An AI-governance readiness check for SMEs and the advisors, law firms and ecosystem partners that support them: a governance score, an executive snapshot and a board report.

public.fact: Offers an AI Governance Readiness Check that assesses governance maturity, identifies risks and generates 'practical, defensible outputs in days instead of months'.
Serves two audiences: SMEs using AI but unsure about the risks, and ecosystem partners 'supporting hundreds of SMEs with one scalable intelligent governance tool'.

Plans: Essentials (a 10-minute assessment, a governance score, an initial executive snapshot); Professional (adds a 30-minute review call and an initial executive board report); Partner Licensing (custom, for firms that monitor AI governance across clients).

Says it combines AI governance, regulatory and legal risk, AI assurance and audit readiness, human rights and ethical safeguards, public policy, and SME operational realities, where most solutions cover only one of legal, technical or policy.

The check aims to move an organisation from 'We think our AI is governed' to 'We can demonstrate our AI is governed operationally and defensibly', looking at accountability, oversight, monitoring and evidence readiness.
It says it follows the main UK and EU regulators relevant to AI, and offers real-time diagnostics when a company changes its strategy.
Operated by SUSTAIN-NOBILITY Advisory Ltd, registered in England and Wales.

told: It is selecting 15 pilot startups and is looking for design partners.
Both sides agreed the public company information can be published as a case study.

help.pitch: Sustain-Nobility assesses whether an organisation's AI governance can be demonstrated; RiskMandate measures, per agent, what it was asked to do, what it can actually reach, and the gap. Its assessments ask for evidence; we produce evidence, read-only, as a written record.
mandate: A readiness check states what each AI system is for and who is accountable: that is the mandate, in writing.
reach: Its public pages do not say how the reach of an organisation's agents (credentials, tools, data) is measured: unknown, and where RiskMandate's measurement fits.
gap: Its own words: from 'we think' to 'we can demonstrate'. The gap between mandate and reach, measured per agent, is that demonstration for agentic AI.

together.title: The evidence layer for its assessments
together.text: RiskMandate's mandate, reach and gap record as evidence behind a readiness score, for clients that run AI agents.

together.title: Its pilot, with our agents as a design partner
together.text: Our own agent swarm, with its policies and runs public, as a pilot subject that gives feedback on the check.

together.title: Refer clients both ways
together.text: Its SMEs with agents to RiskMandate for measurement; our contacts that need a governance programme to Sustain-Nobility.

partners.name: Cycubix

asked.by: Dinis, met at the summit; relayed by attendees.1.fringe@PrompTugal.dinis

partners.one_line: A Dublin cybersecurity and GRC consultancy and training company; its first product, ConsentScan, scans websites for cookie and consent violations, with an MCP server on its Pro plan.

public.fact: Cycubix offers cybersecurity training (secure coding in several languages, threat modeling, secure coding for AI and LLM applications against the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs) and consultancy (risk reviews, ISO 27001, GDPR, SOC, NIS2, vCISO).
ConsentScan, by Cycubix Ltd, Dublin, is a GDPR and ePrivacy cookie consent checker: one free scan with no sign-up, about 4 minutes, graded A to F.
A scan loads the site like a first-time EU visitor, records what fires before consent, then clicks Reject and checks whether trackers keep firing.
ConsentScan started as a check Cycubix ran during its ISO 27001, GDPR and security engagements.

Plans: Free (1 scan); Starter €19 a month (1 monitored domain); Pro €39 a month (3 monitored domains, and an MCP server to run scans from Claude, Cursor or any MCP client); Agency €99 (10 domains); Enterprise on request.

Its EU Consent Index (2 Nov 2026) tested 160 leading websites in eight EU countries: 69% loaded trackers or non-essential cookies before consent, and 58% of the sites where a Reject click could be completed kept tracking afterwards.

told: Both sides agreed the public company information can be published as a case study.

help.pitch: ConsentScan measures the gap between what a site says (its consent banner) and what it does (the trackers that fire). RiskMandate measures the same kind of gap for AI agents: what an agent was asked to do against what it can reach. For ConsentScan's own agentic workflow and its MCP server, RiskMandate would write down the mandate, measure the reach and record the gap.
mandate: The scanner's own job: load a site, record cookies, click Reject, grade. A narrow, writable mandate.
reach: Its MCP server lets Claude, Cursor or any MCP client run scans: an outside agent with a tool. What the MCP server's credentials can reach beyond scanning is unknown from public pages.
gap: Unknown from public pages; the mandate is narrow, so the gap is measurable. 'Installed, not blocking' (its words for consent platforms) is the same shape as an agent policy that exists but is not enforced.

together.title: A mandate for the ConsentScan MCP server
together.text: A written mandate for what an agent may do through the MCP server, and its reach measured against it.

together.title: Same pattern, two layers: a joint story
together.text: Banner versus trackers, and mandate versus reach: the same gap, said versus done, for websites and for agents.

together.title: Training meets measurement
together.text: Its secure-coding-for-LLM training and RiskMandate's measurement of the agents those teams build.

partners.name: Oppy

asked.by: Dinis, met at the summit; relayed by attendees.1.fringe@PrompTugal.dinis

partners.one_line: A B2B platform for sales teams: it filters market signals in real time, matches them to the client's ideal customer profile, and drafts outreach for the moment a prospect is likely to buy.

public.fact: Describes itself as identifying 'high-interest B2B leads through real-time signal analysis for context-driven outreach'.

'Oppy continuously filters market signals in real time so you reach the right companies at the exact moment they need you'; every signal is matched against the client's ICP, geography, competitors and roles.
Signals named on the site include hiring spikes, funding rounds, G2 intent, licence approvals, compliance deadlines, breach disclosures, CISO moves and new certifications.

Its terms list the service as identifying companies that match the client's ICP using AI models, analysing market data, and creating draft prospecting messages with AI based on the detected intent signals.
Plans: Starter Pack from €499 a month (unlimited leads, one workspace, CRM sync and enriched context); Custom for larger GTM orgs (intent data, API access, 3+ workspaces, custom agentic workflows).
Its privacy notice lists sub-processors for LLM access, embeddings, a proprietary model, EU hosting (Frankfurt), contact enrichment, LinkedIn and WhatsApp messaging, and workflow automation.
Operated by K AI SUPERINTELLIGENCE, S.L., Barcelona, Spain, under the GDPR and Spain's data protection law.

told: Its agents analyse market signals together with the client's own data to judge whether a prospect is a good fit and whether it is the right moment to sell.
The company gave its name and site for publication when asked.

help.pitch: Oppy's agents read market signals and the client's own data, and draft outreach. RiskMandate would write down each agent's mandate (which data, which tools, which messages it may send), measure what its credentials actually reach (the CRM, enrichment providers, LinkedIn and WhatsApp messaging), and record the gap, as evidence Oppy can hand to its own customers.
mandate: Its stated job: match signals to an ICP, judge timing, draft messages. A draft is a mandate to write, not to send.
reach: CRM sync, enrichment of professional emails and phones, LinkedIn and WhatsApp messaging and workflow automation sit in the same product (its plans and privacy notice). What each agent's credentials can reach in a customer's CRM is unknown from public pages.
gap: Unknown from public pages. The place to look: an agent that may draft but can reach a send path, and an agent deployed into a customer's environment holding that customer's data.

together.title: Lock down their own agents
together.text: A written mandate per Oppy agent, its reach measured against it, and the gap recorded (Dinis's first point).

together.title: Evidence for their customers
together.text: A record that shows customers a tight agentic workflow: what each agent may do with their CRM and data, and what it can actually reach (Dinis's second point).

together.title: Secure the agents they deploy into customers' environments
together.text: Agents that run inside a customer's systems to collect data, each with a mandate and a measured reach (Dinis's third point).

partners.name: Portstone

asked.by: Dinis, met at the summit; relayed by attendees.1.fringe@PrompTugal.dinis

partners.domain_note: No domain was given. portstone.io ('Portstone · Cold calling agency') matches the service described; portstone.com and portstone.co.uk are unrelated paving companies. Not yet confirmed by the company.
partners.one_line: A cold-calling agency: it assigns trained callers to a B2B campaign and runs it end to end, from the target list to the meetings on the client's calendar.

public.fact: Describes itself as a cold calling agency that assigns trained callers to a campaign and runs it end to end, from the target list to the meetings on the client's calendar.
Services: outbound strategy, list building, script writing, SDR placement and training, cold calling, and weekly campaign reporting.
Every call on every campaign is recorded; recordings come with the weekly report, attached to the record they belong to.
Works backwards from the client's revenue goal to the dial volume and connect rate needed, and checks every row of a list for the right company, person and role before calling.
Pricing per campaign: Starter $2,000 (500 dials), Growth $3,500 (1,000 dials), Scale $5,000 (1,500 dials, multiple callers), Custom on request; no setup fees, no long-term contract.
Says it has called into law, agency, B2B SaaS, consulting, salestech, recruiting, financial advisory and other markets, and does not guarantee meetings.
Its callers are people, selected, trained and managed by Portstone; the site names no AI agents in its own process.

told: A fractional SDR and cold-calling service that builds outbound pipeline for B2B tech companies.

help.pitch: Portstone's own work is done by people, not AI agents, so RiskMandate's measurement is not the first fit. The fit Dinis sees is the other way round: Portstone as an outbound phone channel for RiskMandate's agent-risk assessments and the summit packages, calling B2B tech companies that run AI agents.
mandate: Unknown for agents: the site describes human callers working from an approved script and list. The script is a written mandate for a caller.
reach: Its process touches client target lists, call recordings and CRM-style records. Whether any AI tooling sits behind list sourcing or connect-rate optimisation is unknown from public pages.
gap: Unknown. If Portstone adds AI to list sourcing, dialling or reporting, the mandate, reach and gap measurement applies there.

together.title: An outbound phone channel for RiskMandate
together.text: Portstone calls B2B tech companies to book meetings for RiskMandate's agent-risk assessments and the summit packages (Dinis's point): a reseller or pipeline partner.

together.title: A script built from the X-ray and GAMMA-Ray
together.text: Calls that open with what we already published about the prospect's agents: our partner briefs and X-rays as the call research.

together.title: Measure it like a campaign
together.text: Its own funnel (dials, connects, completions, leads, meetings) reported weekly against the summit offer.
